encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe lower abdominal pain after vigorous exercise with nausea

lines: Sudden onset of severe lower abdominal pain after vigorous exercise with nausea

The patient is a 31-year-old female with essential hypertension, Rh(D)-negative blood type, and history of ruptured hepatocellular adenoma (January 2020) who returns to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe lower abdominal pain that started 4 hours ago after a session of vigorous exercise.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant, with some intermittent cramping.
She also reports nausea but no vomiting.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and temperature 37.2°C (99°F)
Abdominal examination reveals diffuse tenderness, marked rigidity, and rebound tenderness.
A pelvic examination is deferred due to severe abdominal pain.
Laboratory tests show a hemoglobin level of 11.2 g/dL (baseline 13.5 g/dL), white blood cell count of 12,000/uL, and a negative pregnancy test.
An ultrasound of the pelvis shows free fluid in the cul-de-sac.
The patient becomes progressively tachycardic and her blood pressure drops to 85/55 mmHg despite fluid resuscitation.

encounters.cc: Dizziness and fatigue following motor vehicle collision with mild abdominal pain

lines: Dizziness and fatigue following motor vehicle collision with mild abdominal pain
She presents after a motor vehicle collision with history of ruptured hepatocellular adenoma (2020) and corpus luteum cyst (2021).
She reports that she was the restrained driver in a head-on collision at moderate speed.
Airbags were deployed, and she did not lose consciousness.
She complains of mild abdominal pain but no other specific injuries.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
Vital signs reveal a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg, heart rate of 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 97% on room air.
On examination, she is alert but appears pale and anxious.
Her skin is cool and clammy.
The abdominal examination shows mild tenderness in the left upper quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Pelvic and rectal examinations are unremarkable.
There is no external evidence of trauma.
Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) exam is negative for free fluid in the abdomen.

encounters.cc: Acute onset of lower abdominal pain and vaginal spotting with 6 weeks gestation

lines: Acute onset of lower abdominal pain and vaginal spotting with 6 weeks gestation

This 33-year-old Rh(D)-negative female with essential hypertension and prior emergency presentations for ruptured hepatocellular adenoma, ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum, and hypovolemic shock presents with acute abdominal complaints.
She reports that the pain is sharp, located on the left side, and began suddenly 6 hours ago.
She also mentions that she has been feeling light-headed and has had some vaginal spotting over the past day.
Her last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago, and she has a history of irregular menstrual cycles.
She is sexually active with one partner and does not use contraception.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
Her past medical history is significant for a blood transfusion following a motor vehicle accident 5 years ago, after which she was told she has an Rh(D)-negative blood type.
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
Blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 110 beats per minute
On examination, she appears pale. A pelvic examination reveals left adnexal tenderness.
A urine pregnancy test is positive.
Hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL, hematocrit is 29.4%, and blood type is confirmed to be O negative.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterine cavity and a left adnexal mass with surrounding free fluid.

encounters.cc: Regular contractions every 5 minutes for 2 hours at 30 weeks gestation without rupture of membranes

lines: Regular contractions every 5 minutes for 2 hours at 30 weeks gestation without rupture of membranes
This 33-year-old Rh(D)-negative female with ruptured hepatic adenoma, ruptured luteum cyst, and first-trimester bleeding presents with regular contractions.
She reports no rupture of membranes or vaginal bleeding.
Her previous pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she delivered a healthy full-term infant.
Her current pregnancy has been uneventful until now.
She is currently at 30 weeks gestation.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F)
Fetal heart tones are 140 beats per minute.
A speculum examination reveals a closed cervical os.
Transabdominal ultrasound shows a normal amount of amniotic fluid with no fetal anomalies.
Given the patient's gestational age and symptoms, the decision is made to initiate tocolysis.

encounters.cc: Sudden gush of clear fluid from the vagina while doing household chores at 34 weeks gestation

lines: Sudden gush of clear fluid from the vagina while doing household chores at 34 weeks gestation

The patient is a 33-year-old Rh(D)-negative female with a history of threatened preterm labor who returns to the emergency department with a complaint of sudden gush of clear fluid from the vagina while doing household chores.
She denies any contractions, vaginal bleeding, or abdominal pain.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
Her previous pregnancy was uneventful, and she had a vaginal delivery at term.
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
On examination, her vital signs are stable, and the fetal heart rate is 140 beats per minute.
Speculum examination confirms pooling of clear fluid in the vaginal vault.
Nitrazine paper test turns blue, and ferning is observed under the microscope.
The patient is admitted for inpatient management.

lines: Regular contractions every 5 minutes with rupture of membranes 30 minutes ago at 36 weeks gestation
This 34-year-old has a history of threatened preterm labor at 30 weeks and preterm premature rupture of membranes at 34 weeks during this pregnancy.
Her prenatal course was unremarkable except for a positive group B Streptococcus (GBS) screen at 36 weeks.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
Her past medical history is significant for a rash following penicillin administration as a child, which she describes as "hives all over the body.".
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
She denies any respiratory distress, facial swelling, or previous anaphylaxis.
On examination, her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
The fetal heart rate tracing is reassuring. The patient's cervix is dilated to 4 cm.
The obstetric team is preparing for intrapartum management.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding during labor

lines: Sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding during labor

The patient is a 34-year-old Rh(D)-negative female with a history of ruptured hepatocellular adenoma, ruptured corpus luteum cyst, and hypovolemic shock who was admitted earlier today in active labor and now presents with sudden-onset severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding during labor.
She reports that the pain is sharp and constant.
- Ruptured corpus luteum cyst with hemoperitoneum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Group B Streptococcus Colonization in Pregnancy with Non-Severe Penicillin Allergy (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
Her past obstetric history is significant for two prior cesarean deliveries, the last of which was a classical cesarean section due to a transverse lie.
- Cesarean section x2 (last procedure: classical uterine incision)
- Partial hepatectomy for ruptured hepatic mass
- Laparoscopic evacuation of hemoperitoneum with right ovarian cystectomy
- Blood transfusion (packed red blood cells) following motor vehicle collision
- Oral contraceptive pills (combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) 1 tablet by mouth daily (continuous use for 10 years)
On examination, her vital signs are: blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, heart rate 110 bpm, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F).
The abdomen is tender to palpation with a palpable irregular mass noted on the right side.
There is no evidence of placental abruption on ultrasound, and the placenta is noted to be in the posterior position.
Fetal heart tones are irregular, with variable decelerations noted on the cardiotocography.
